tasks.title: ngv2/poc_authenticity_gate.py -- pure deterministic AST PoC authenticity classifier (forbids confirmed verdict for self-contained mocks)
acceptance_criteria: NEW file ngv2/poc_authenticity_gate.py exists and is importable as `from ngv2.poc_authenticity_gate import classify_poc_authenticity`.
Primary function has the EXACT signature `classify_poc_authenticity(poc_source: str, target_import_names: list[str]) -> dict`.

Return value is a dict with EXACTLY the keys {mode, imports_target, defines_vuln_locally, issues_network_request, may_confirm}; mode is one of {real_target, self_contained_mock, network_live}; the other four are bools; may_confirm == (mode != 'self_contained_mock').
Edge case (a): a PoC that imports a name in target_import_names and references it -> mode == 'real_target', imports_target == True, may_confirm == True.

Edge case (b): a PoC that defines its OWN def vulnerable_route(...)/mock handler class and imports nothing from the target -> mode == 'self_contained_mock', defines_vuln_locally == True, imports_target == False, may_confirm == False.

Edge case (c): a PoC that spins up a localhost mock server and hits it with requests but imports nothing from the target -> issues_network_request == True yet mode == 'self_contained_mock', may_confirm == False.
Edge case (d): empty or syntactically-garbage poc_source -> mode == 'self_contained_mock', may_confirm == False.
Module is PURE and stdlib-only (ast + typing): no network, disk I/O, clock, randomness, uuid, subprocess, MCP, third-party import, or import of any sibling ngv2/** leaf.

AST-safety: sink/library names (eval, exec, requests, socket, urllib, etc.) appear ONLY as string-literal data and comments; NO eval/exec/__import__/os.system/subprocess CALL and NO decorator anywhere in the module.
Determinism: identical inputs yield byte-identical output dicts.
The committed oracle tests/ngv2/test_poc_authenticity_gate_wired.py is GREEN under `python3 -m pytest -q tests/ngv2/test_poc_authenticity_gate_wired.py`.

spec.objective: Create the NEW pure, deterministic, stdlib-only module ngv2/poc_authenticity_gate.py that statically classifies a PoC's source TEXT into mode in {real_target, self_contained_mock, network_live} and returns may_confirm=False for self-contained mocks, so the NobleGreed verdict path can refuse to emit 'confirmed' for PoCs that mock/reimplement the target instead of exercising the real software. The module never runs/imports/execs the PoC; it only parses the source with ast and inspects the tree.
functional_requirements: Parse poc_source exactly once with ast.parse; an empty source or a source that raises SyntaxError is treated as a self-contained mock (it cannot be shown to exercise the real target), yielding mode='self_contained_mock' and may_confirm=False without raising.

Compute imports_target=True iff the PoC import-statements or from-import statements bring in any name in target_import_names (matched by top-level package OR any dotted prefix) AND that imported name is referenced somewhere in the module body (not merely imported and unused).

Compute issues_network_request=True iff the PoC makes an outbound HTTP/socket call via requests, urllib/urllib.request, http.client, or socket (detected from the imported names and their call sites in the AST).

Compute defines_vuln_locally=True iff the PoC defines its OWN functions or classes that stand in for the vulnerable behavior (e.g. a def vulnerable_route(...), a mock handler/class, or a locally started server) AND does NOT import the target.

Derive mode = 'real_target' when imports_target else 'network_live' when issues_network_request and not imports_target and not merely a local mock else 'self_contained_mock'; set may_confirm = (mode != 'self_contained_mock'); return a fixed-shape dict with EXACTLY the keys {mode, imports_target, defines_vuln_locally, issues_network_request, may_confirm} deterministically (byte-identical for identical inputs).
spec.interfaces: Public: classify_poc_authenticity(poc_source: str, target_import_names: list[str]) -> dict. Returns dict with EXACTLY keys: mode (str in {'real_target','self_contained_mock','network_live'}), imports_target (bool), defines_vuln_locally (bool), issues_network_request (bool), may_confirm (bool). Stdlib imports limited to `ast` and `typing`. No other public symbols required; any helpers are private (underscore-prefixed) module-level functions. Consumed downstream by the verdict path via `from ngv2.poc_authenticity_gate import classify_poc_authenticity` (wiring is OUT OF SCOPE here).
edge_cases: (a) imports + references a target name -> real_target / imports_target True / may_confirm True.
(b) defines own def vulnerable_route(...) or mock handler class, imports nothing from target -> self_contained_mock / defines_vuln_locally True / imports_target False / may_confirm False.
(c) localhost mock server hit via requests, no target import -> issues_network_request True but mode still self_contained_mock / may_confirm False (network targets its own mock).
(d) empty string or syntactically-garbage source -> self_contained_mock / may_confirm False, no exception raised.
Target name matched by dotted prefix (e.g. target 'pkg' matches `import pkg.sub` and `from pkg.sub import x`).
Imported-but-unused target name -> imports_target False (must be referenced in the body).
A PoC that both imports the target AND issues a network request -> mode='real_target' (imports_target wins over network_live).
non_goals: Do NOT run, import, exec, or detonate the PoC source -- only static classification of source TEXT.

Do NOT wire this classifier into the live verdict/detonation path, detonation chamber, selection_ranker, or any other existing module (separate downstream EDIT leaf). integration with the verdict pipeline is excluded; because this is a pure self-contained classifier with no live call site of its own, the integration-test requirement is excused.
Do NOT author or modify any test other than the committed oracle.
Do NOT add real network, disk I/O, clock, randomness, subprocess, or logging.
Do NOT import any third-party package or any sibling ngv2/** leaf.
Do NOT introduce any eval/exec/__import__/os.system/subprocess CALL or any decorator -- sink/library names live ONLY as string-literal data/comments.
spec.implementation_notes:
Single-file WHOLE-FILE emission. Top: `import ast` and `from typing import ...`. Wrap ast.parse in try/except SyntaxError; also short-circuit on empty/whitespace-only source -> mock result. Walk the tree once collecting: (1) imported aliases from ast.Import/ast.ImportFrom (track both module root and dotted prefixes and the local bound names/asnames), (2) all Name/Attribute references to test usage, (3) network library imports (requests, urllib, urllib.request, http.client, socket) and whether they appear in Call nodes, (4) locally-defined FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef/ClassDef names matching vulnerability/mock/server/handler/route heuristics (e.g. names containing 'vuln', 'mock', 'handler', 'route', 'server', or starting an HTTPServer/BaseHTTPRequestHandler subclass). imports_target requires BOTH a matching import AND a body reference of the bound name. Match target names by top-level package equality OR dotted-prefix (split on '.'). Build mode per the precedence in FR5. Return the dict with keys in a fixed insertion order so output is byte-stable. Keep all sink/library identifiers as string constants compared against AST-extracted names -- never call them. No decorators (incl. @staticmethod/@property); use plain module-level functions only. Make the committed oracle tests/ngv2/test_poc_authenticity_gate_wired.py GREEN.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Inline PoC source-string fixtures covering: (a) `import <target>; <target>.do()` style real-target PoC; (b) a self-contained script defining `def vulnerable_route(...)` and/or a mock handler class with no target import; (c) a localhost mock server (e.g. http.server) hit via `requests.get('http://127.0.0.1...')` with no target import; (d) empty string '' and an unparsable garbage string; plus an imported-but-unused-target sample, a dotted-prefix import sample, and a sample importing both target and a network lib. All fixtures are plain Python string literals; no external files, network, or runtime execution of the PoC source.

token_budget_ratio.note: Implementation is a single bounded stdlib-only AST classifier; the committed oracle is authoritative and must not be re-authored, but the spec enumerates ample unit/property/regression coverage, so test reasoning budget exceeds implementation per the 1.5x rule.
